event: Elsie wakes in the attic room to bread-smell and lake mist on the round window.

memory.fact: The Honeycomb's attic is one narrow room with a sloped ceiling and a round window over the canal.

pictured.coverAfter: The room was a narrow strip under the roof, the round window pale with mist.

event: She greets her four potted plants by name, then washes at the cold basin.

memory.fact: Elsie's houseplants travel with her in a crate, and every one has a name.

pictured.coverAfter: She said good morning to her four plants by name.

event: She laces her novice's cream halter, hands unsteady, and clips the flower above one ear.

changes.note: Elsie laces on the novice's outfit: now worn
Flower clip set above her left ear: now worn

pictured.coverAfter: The novice's outfit lay folded on the stool.
pictured.outfit: cropped cream halter top, short sage-green skirt, brown belt with pouches, fingerless gloves and tall boots

event: She counts her coins and packs the satchel: salve, bandages.

changes.note: Elsie counts her coins on the bed: 13 lanterns, 4 pips

event: Elsie eats a warm roll at the bakery, and the baker waves her out.
She posts the letter at the corner shop; two women go by arm in arm.

pictured.coverAfter: She posted the letter to her mother at the corner shop, and on the way

event: The Hall of Naming stands white above the lake, its glass dome full of morning.

memory.fact: The Hall of Naming is a white stone hall with a glass dome, on the lakeshore.

pictured.coverAfter: The Hall of Naming stood at the end of the lakeshore road, white stone

event: The girl ahead asks if she is nervous; Elsie says yes, and warms her cold hands.
Inside, a priestess calls the names; the first girl's window opens above her.

memory.fact: A priestess of the Hall calls each name, and each steps alone into a silver circle in the floor.
The System's window opens in the air above the circle, and the whole hall can read it.

event: Elsie hopes for simples; then her turn comes, and she steps into the circle.
It reads: Enthraller.

changes.note: Class: Enthraller, read in the Hall's window

memory.fact: Elsie Fairweather's class is Enthraller.

event: She reads it twice; the silence spreads outward and nobody in the hall moves.

memory.fact: Lanternmere still whispers of Vesper Locke and the War of Strings at the word Enthraller.

event: A woman in the gallery rises and walks out; the priestess calls no next name.

memory.fact: A woman in a good dark coat walked out of the gallery when Elsie was named Enthraller.
A woman in a good dark coat walked out of the gallery when Elsie was named Enthraller.
A woman in a good dark coat walked out of the gallery when Elsie was named Enthraller.

event: Elsie says, Oh! that sounds like a lot of responsibility, and steps down.
The hall does not clap; outside, the others from the line look at her and away.
She walks down from the hall alone, and the city is warm and ordinary around her.

memory.fact: Elsie's eyes fill easily, at kindness as readily as at sorrow.

event: The guild hall is timber and noise, its green copper roof across Brightwater Square.

memory.fact: The guild hall is a great timber hall with a green copper roof on Brightwater Square.

pictured.coverAfter: The guild hall stood across Brightwater Square under a green copper roof,

event: In the registration line, the clerk takes her name and asks her class.
She says Enthraller; the clerk's pen stops, and he goes up the stairs.
The guildmaster comes down, grey and sword-calloused, and takes Elsie up.

memory.fact: The guildmaster is a grey-haired retired A-rank swordswoman in her fifties, with an office upstairs.

event: She reads the Strings Accord: every skill reported, none on anyone unwilling.

memory.fact: Under the Strings Accord every Enthraller is registered with the guild and watched by a Warden.
An Enthraller's Warden writes down every skill she uses and reports it to the guildmaster.
Under the Accord an Enthraller may use a skill on no one who has not agreed, unless it saves a life.

event: Told the watching is so nothing goes wrong, Elsie says she is glad of it.
She counts the fee onto the desk; the clerk stamps a copper tag with an F.

changes.note: F-rank: the clerk stamps an F on her copper tag
Guild fee of two silver lanterns paid: 134 → 114 pips
Fee paid: Elsie ends the chapter with 114 pips

memory.fact: Registering costs two lanterns, and each adventurer gets a copper rank tag stamped with her name.

event: In the main hall, the guildmaster opens a charcoal door: a young woman with a ledger.

memory.fact: The guild's Wardens keep a room off the main hall, behind a charcoal-painted door.

pictured.coverAfter: Then the guildmaster walked her back along the hall to a door painted
pictured.outfit: charcoal guild coat buttoned to the throat, slim dark trousers and black boots

event: Warden Corisande Vane, called Cora, will go with her and write down every skill.

memory.fact: Cora is the Warden who goes with Elsie and writes down every skill she uses.
Cora is the Warden who goes with Elsie and writes down every skill she uses.
Cora is the Warden who goes with Elsie and writes down every skill she uses.
Cora is the Warden who goes with Elsie and writes down every skill she uses.

event: Cora will report each to the guildmaster; Elsie thanks her for coming.
Cora does not answer; Elsie asks what she likes in her tea.
Cora says: black and strong, one sugar; Elsie says she will remember it.
Back in the hall, Elsie reads the F-rank notices, then finds the party board.

memory.fact: The party board is where parties chalk their names on slates and seek adventurers to fill them.

event: Parties look each other over and nobody looks at her; the slates she asks are full.
The fourth slate is turned to the wall; the cast-offs' slates stand at the corner.
A woman with a great axe strapped across her back is arguing at one of them.

pictured.coverAfter: She was tall and lean, with a great axe strapped across her back,
pictured.outfit: sleeveless battered leather jerkin, knuckle wraps, dark trousers and scuffed boots

event: She offers Elsie the half of her slate she has not used; the axe is Margery.
The Copper Hounds dropped Tamsin this morning, over the shield-bearer's arm.
Elsie's hand goes flat on Tamsin's wrist; Tamsin goes still, and her ears are red.
Elsie asks whether the arm is mending; Tamsin stares, and says probably.
A small woman in brass goggles, Ottilie Brandt called Tilly, comes out talking fast.

pictured.coverAfter: It was a small woman with brass goggles pushed up into her hair,
pictured.outfit: cream blouse with rolled sleeves, too-big scorched apron and a belt of corked vials

event: Thrown out of the Alchemists' College, she answers what she brews with three warnings.

memory.fact: Tilly Brandt is an Alchemist of F-rank.
Tilly registered with the guild three days ago, and no party has taken her.
Tilly registered with the guild three days ago, and no party has taken her.
The Alchemists' College threw Tilly out last week, after her brew blew out its east lab windows.
The Alchemists' College threw Tilly out last week, after her brew blew out its east lab windows.

event: Tilly goes red to the ears when Elsie smiles, and drops her chalk twice.
Tamsin's guild notice: six lanterns for the apothecary, moonbells at the Glasswood.

memory.fact: On the F-rank board today: moonbells from the Glasswood's edge for an apothecary, six lanterns.

event: Elsie says the three could take it, split three ways; Tamsin asks if she has been in a dungeon.

memory.fact: Elsie has never been inside a dungeon.
Elsie has never been inside a dungeon.

event: Elsie chalks three names on the last slate; Tilly writes hers under, then Tamsin.

memory.fact: Elsie, Tamsin and Ottilie Brandt chalked their names on the last slate as a party.
Elsie, Tamsin and Ottilie Brandt chalked their names on the last slate as a party.
Elsie, Tamsin and Ottilie Brandt chalked their names on the last slate as a party.
Elsie, Tamsin and Ottilie Brandt chalked their names on the last slate as a party.

event: Tilly asks her class; Elsie says Enthraller and does not look away.
Tamsin says, so you can make me do anything; Elsie says she has never used it on anyone.

memory.fact: Elsie has never once used her class to make anyone feel anything.

event: Tilly asks about bonds; Cora watches the wrist, the chalk, the red ears, and writes nothing.

changes.note: Bond: Tamsin 15 (the wrist, the arm, the slate)
Bond: Tilly 10 (her red ears, the chalk)

event: Somebody brings bread and a jug, and the four of them eat standing at the board.
Tamsin says moonbells open at dusk, so they will go out at dusk tomorrow.

memory.fact: Moonbells open all together at dusk, and are shut again by midnight.
Moonbells open all together at dusk, and are shut again by midnight.
Moonbells open all together at dusk, and are shut again by midnight.

event: Elsie thinks the three of them are going to be friends, and is glad enough to hum.

memory.fact: Elsie reads the ache of wanting someone near as friendship, and files every girl's love so.
Now and then Elsie hums without knowing it.

event: The lamplighters' boats move along the canal, and the lanterns come on one by one.

memory.fact: Paper lanterns hang along every canal, and lamplighters' boats light them at dusk.

event: Cora opens the black ledger, writes nothing, and puts it back under her coat.
Asked what she will write, Cora says she has not decided.

memory.fact: Cora has not decided what to write in her ledger about Elsie.
Cora has not decided what to write in her ledger about Elsie.

event: Elsie says she will try to give her something good to write.
